Raise HEAD_LR to 0.65 and lower BIAS_LR to 0.05 as a small retune of the SGD groups.
Remove the dirac_ identity init from Conv.reset_parameters so convs use the default PyTorch init.

Apply brightness/contrast jitter to each indexed batch instead of the full 50000-image epoch tensor.
Disable brightness/contrast color jitter in the training augmentation.
Use 480 instead of 960 training images for the whitening init to make patch extraction and SVD slightly cheaper.
Train the first 40% of steps on bilinearly downsampled 24x24 batches, then 32x32, using adaptive max pooling so the head stays valid.
Pass the per-step target magnitude as a tensor instead of the Python int step count, so the compiled Newton-Schulz function is not recompiled every step and no longer hits the cache size limit.
Keep a decay-0.9 EMA of params and BN stats over the last 25% of steps, copy it into the model at the end of train(), and cut EPOCHS to 7.25.
Reduce block2/block3 widths from 256 to 192, raise EPOCHS to 7.9 and MUON_LR by 1.1x (0.205 to 0.2255).
Replace the reflect-pad plus gather crop with torch.roll of 5 contiguous chunks by random (dy,dx) shifts in [-2,2] each epoch.

issues: No sign of getting around the measurement. The diff carries no state from one run to the next, does no work in the untimed first call, sets no seeds, does not use the test images and has no file access.

No bug that makes the result meaningless. Removing one unrolled Newton-Schulz iteration from Muon's orthogonalisation is a real algorithmic change: it trades orthogonalisation quality for speed. The code that remains (the `A = X @ X^T`, `B`, `X` update) is still well formed. Only part of the function is visible, so I cannot check whether a comment or iteration count elsewhere still says 5 steps. That would be cosmetic only.

The result agrees with the reported decision. Candidate cost is 0.2988 against the incumbent's -0.0907, which is much worse. Most likely the accuracy loss from the less exact orthogonalisation outweighs the time saved, and raising MUON_LR to 0.215 did not make up for it. Reject is correct.

z recomputed with the per-job noise sd of 0.026 and one run on each side: (-0.0907 - 0.2988) / (0.026 * sqrt(2)) ≈ -10.59. The harness reports -10.677, which implies an sd of about 0.0365, so it probably uses a slightly different variance estimate. The two agree in size and sign.
Both sides have only one run, so z depends entirely on the assumed noise sd. Even so, the gap is about 15 times the single-job sd, so the decision does not depend on that assumption.

description: Drop the third Newton-Schulz iteration in Muon and raise MUON_LR by 5 percent to compensate.
Downsample training batches to 20x20 instead of 24x24 for the first 30% of steps to speed up early training.
Change the BatchNorm default momentum argument from 0.5566 to 0.45 so the running stats follow the recent weights more closely.
Set WHITEN_BIAS_EPOCHS to 0.1 so the whitening bias is frozen after fewer steps.
Reduce block2 and block3 widths from 256 to 224 to cut conv FLOPs, with no compensation.
